purpose: Country-specific agricultural evidence inventory for later validation; not a production calculator profile.

sections.source_name: FAO/WFP Crop and Food Security Assessment Mission 2025; Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security release
sections.reference_date: Report published 19 March 2026; Ministry launch 31 March 2026

observations.item: Net cereal production in traditional smallholder sector
observations.finding: Estimated 8 percent above 2024 output and 27 percent above the previous five-year average.

caveats: This is an aggregate cereal production estimate, not crop-specific production, area or yield.
Do not divide national output by a generic land-area estimate to create yields.
Extract the full CFSAM tables by crop, state and season before setting crop-level calculator parameters.

sections.topic: current crop season, rainfall and production risks
sections.source_name: FAO GIEWS South Sudan Country Brief

observations.item: 2026 first-season maize and sorghum harvest in southern agricultural areas
observations.finding: Below-average rainfall and prolonged dry spells affected crop establishment and development; output was expected below average.

observations.item: Northern and central short-cycle cereal harvest
observations.finding: Short-cycle sorghum and maize harvesting had started; long-cycle sorghum was expected to be gathered November 2026 to January 2027.

observations.item: Second-season crop outlook in southern areas
observations.finding: Forecast above-average October–December rainfall could support second-season crops and yields, subject to actual weather and security conditions.

caveats: The 2026 outlook is provisional and must not be treated as final harvest data.
South Sudan has distinct bimodal southern and unimodal central/northern crop calendars; a single national season assumption is inappropriate.
Conflict and insecurity disrupted agricultural activities in some areas.

sections.topic: crop portfolio and agricultural production geography
sections.source_name: FAO/WFP CFSAM 2025; CLIMIS South Sudan market and livelihood information

observations.finding: Maize and sorghum are central cereal crops; millet and other cereals also appear in the national statistical and market-data sources.

CLIMIS price-monitoring catalogue includes groundnuts, cowpea, sesame, dried cassava, Irish potatoes and pulses; presence in the market list is a candidate crop lead, not proof of national production scale.
Southern areas include first- and second-season crop cycles, while central and northern areas rely more heavily on a main rainy season and short-/long-cycle sorghum and maize.

caveats: The crop list is a research shortlist, not a validated 17-crop national calculator profile.
Validate each crop's producing states, area, harvested area, season and yield against the detailed CFSAM and national survey tables.
Do not infer farm profitability from the presence of a commodity in a market-price database.

sections.topic: market price series and commodity coverage
sections.source_name: CLIMIS South Sudan market information system, supported by MAFS, WFP and partners
sections.reference_date: Market dashboard accessed 2026-11-01; selectable historical series 2009–2026

observations.finding: The dashboard identifies MAFS, WFP, Concern Worldwide, FEWS NET and other partners as market-price data contributors; it provides state, county, commodity and period filters.

Weekly catalogue includes red and white sorghum, white maize, maize and sorghum flour, rice, groundnuts, sesame, cowpea, beans, livestock, milk, fuel, farm casual labour and mechanized/oxen traction hiring.
The catalogue distinguishes grain prices from 50 kg or 90 kg shawal/bag observations for selected cereals; units must be preserved exactly as displayed.

caveats: Dashboard metadata establishes availability, not the current observed price value. Export actual dated state/county/commodity observations before using them.
Most displayed observations are market prices; retail/wholesale prices must not be labelled farmgate producer prices.
Record commodity grade, market, unit, date, currency and source agency for every extracted row.

sections.source_name: WFP Eastern and Southern Africa Office Market and Trade Update, 2025 Q1
sections.reference_date: March 2025 observation, published in 2025 Q1 update

observations.item: Red sorghum retail price in Aweil market
observations.finding: Reported as more than 150 percent higher than the same period a year earlier.

caveats: This is a dated retail market observation, not a current 2026 quote and not a farmgate price.
The malwa unit is 3.5 kg; do not convert to per-kg without preserving the original unit and checking the market series definition.
The report describes substantial regional price variation and macroeconomic/transport constraints.

sections.topic: recent market inflation, price volatility and exchange-rate conditions
sections.source_name: FAO GIEWS FPMA price warning; FEWS NET South Sudan August 2026 outlook update
sections.reference_date: FAO warning 13 October 2026, covering September prices; FEWS NET August 2026

observations.finding: Retail prices remained firm at record levels.
After reaching record highs in June, maize prices declined for a third consecutive month, falling 2 percent in September as first-season harvest supplies increased.
FEWS NET reported an 18 percent loss in SSP purchasing value over the period; it also reported a 23–24 percent year-on-year loss in official and parallel markets.
Prices increased 5–20 percent from June across major markets in the August 2026 update.

caveats: Extreme inflation and exchange-rate instability make undated or unconverted nominal prices unsuitable for a stable calculator input.
Keep official and parallel exchange-rate series separate and record the source/date for any conversion.
A national average must not conceal market-level price dispersion or disrupted trade routes.

sections.source_name: FAO GIEWS South Sudan Country Brief

observations.item: Population facing IPC Phase 3 or worse
observations.finding: About 55 percent of the population was estimated to face Crisis or worse acute food insecurity.
FAO reported approximately 73,000 people in Catastrophe, including 24,000 in Upper Nile and 49,000 in Jonglei.

caveats: Conflict, displacement, flooding history, drought, fuel costs and disrupted trade affect access to land, labour, inputs and markets.
Food-security statistics are not crop-yield or profitability indicators.
Security and access conditions must be evaluated at state/county level before recommending a production enterprise.

sections.topic: national agricultural statistics and validation requirements
sections.source_name: South Sudan National Bureau of Statistics agriculture statistics and survey portal

observations.finding: The NBS portal advertises crop production, livestock, fisheries, agricultural employment and agricultural survey resources, including an Agricultural Survey Report 2024.

caveats: The portal's summary indicators and crop tables require verification against original NBS publications, metadata and the FAO/WFP CFSAM before they are treated as validated national statistics.
No crop-specific yield or cost series has been adopted from the portal summary in this evidence record.
Obtain original survey tables and document sample design, coverage, crop definitions, planted versus harvested area and missing-data treatment.

calculator_data_gaps: Obtain the complete FAO/WFP CFSAM 2025 tables and extract crop-specific area, production and yield by state, county and season.
Verify NBS Agricultural Survey Report 2024 and underlying survey tables against CFSAM estimates; resolve differences in coverage, crop definitions and totals.
Export dated CLIMIS market observations for priority crops and livestock by state/county; preserve retail, wholesale, bag and small local-unit measures.
Collect verified producer/farmgate prices by crop, market, grade, season and date; do not substitute retail sorghum or maize prices.
Collect current seed, fertiliser, crop-protection, land preparation, labour, traction, irrigation, fuel, transport, storage and post-harvest input quotations by production zone.
Build separate budgets for southern bimodal maize/sorghum systems and central/northern cereal systems; do not apply one national yield or cost assumption.
Validate crop presence and production scale for groundnut, sesame, cowpea, cassava, millet and other candidate crops before adding them to a calculator crop list.
Document SSP inflation and official/parallel exchange-rate series with effective dates; never hard-code a stale nominal price.
Assess conflict, displacement, road access, flooding and drought risks by location before assigning representative enterprise assumptions.
Develop livestock budgets separately using species, breed, herd composition, feed, water, veterinary costs, mortality, liveweight, milk yield and market transaction data.

activation_blockers: Crop-specific state/county/season area, production and yield tables have not been extracted and reconciled.
No verified current farmgate producer-price series has been adopted.
No complete regional crop enterprise budgets or current input quotations.
Nominal SSP prices and exchange rates are highly volatile and require dated treatment.
Market access, conflict and climate conditions vary materially by state and county.
NBS portal summary data require validation against original statistical reports and CFSAM.

safeguards: Research-only evidence; not a live calculator dataset.
Do not activate South Sudan or change calculator formulas based on this file.
Do not treat aggregate national cereal production as a crop-specific yield or farm-level production figure.
Do not substitute retail or wholesale market prices for farmgate producer prices.
Preserve local market units such as malwa and shawal alongside any verified conversions.
Keep official and parallel exchange-rate observations distinct and dated.
Do not generalize 2026 drought, conflict or food-security conditions into normal-year enterprise assumptions.
